captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a parametric wine glass holder designed for under-cabinet mounting. It features a long, wedge-shaped main body with a sloped profile that tapers from back to front, creating an ergonomic entry angle for glass bases. The structure is lightened by four large rectangular cutouts along its length, and it includes three blocky mounting legs extending from the thicker back edge, each containing a countersunk screw hole for secure installation.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric wine glass holder in OpenSCAD. The model should feature a main body with a sloped profile, multiple rectangular cutouts for weight reduction, and three mounting legs along the back edge containing countersunk screw holes. Make the overall length, width, height, leg dimensions, and cutout sizes fully adjustable using parameters.
captions.factory: The code constructs the wine glass holder using a boolean difference operation on a base shape. The base is created by unioning a rectangular cube (representing the mounting legs) with a 2D polygon extruded along the length of the holder to form the sloped main body. A series of for-loops then subtract cylindrical screw holes with beveled entries from the mounting legs, two large rectangular cutouts from the front section, and four smaller rectangular air holes from the main body, all positioned dynamically based on calculated offsets.
